column1: # What maps to what: Spring AMQP, the RabbitMQ Java client and JMS onto AceMQ.
# One row per source API. Tab-separated columns:
#   id       stable name of the row, used in the report and the JSON
#   kind     import (matched against import lines) | usage (matched against code, only in a
#            file that imports from the source's packages)
#   step     where it falls in the migration order (1-8, see Steps in Report.java)
#   acemq    the AceMQ equivalent; "none:" means there is no direct one and says what to do
# Deterministic on purpose: the model is asked only about what this table leaves to judgment.

column7: ConnectionConfig + AceMq.connect(config), or the starter's acemq.url
column8: One AceMq per application; it owns its channels, recovery and publisher confirms.
Publishes are confirmed and mandatory by default; an unroutable send fails instead of vanishing.
As RabbitTemplate.
A MessagePostProcessor that sets headers becomes Envelope.header(...).
Replies use direct reply-to; a reply the caller cannot decode fails at once.

column7: none: AceMQ has no polling get; consume the queue (mq.consume) instead
column8: A polling loop becomes a push consumer; check what drove the poll rate.
concurrency and prefetch become @AceListener(concurrency, prefetch).

column7: none: one handler per payload type; dispatch on type inside one AceListener
column8: Multi-method listeners that dispatch on payload class need a small switch.

column7: mq.consume(queue, Type.class, ConsumerOptions.prefetch(n), handler) or mq.consumeGroup(...)
column8: Container concurrency becomes consumeGroup(...).concurrency(n).
Factory-wide settings move to configuration.
Manual channel acks map to AckAwareHandler; most code can drop them.
queueWithDeadLetter(name) declares the queue with its .dlq and .parked.
Plans show drift before anything changes.
Retries move from in-memory sleeps to broker delay queues; nothing sleeps in the consumer thread.
Same intent, explicit names.

column7: Codec (JsonCodec by default; Avro, Protobuf, XML, YAML, TOML codecs)
column8: Check the content type other services send; Jackson2JsonMessageConverter maps to JsonCodec.

column7: none: use the outbox (OutboxRecord + OutboxRelay) for publish-with-database
column8: AMQP transactions are slow and do not span the database; the outbox does.

column7: nothing to write: confirms and mandatory are on by default; Publisher.send fails with PublishFailedException
column8: Delete the callbacks; handle the exception where the send is.
spring.rabbitmq.* properties become acemq.*.
TLS, credentials and recovery are ConnectionConfig settings.

column7: AceMq (one per application); channels are managed for you
column8: Code that shares a Channel across threads is a bug today and goes away.

column7: built in: AceMq recovers connections, channels, consumers and topology
column8: Delete it; recovery is on and tested by the chaos drills.
Arguments such as x-queue-type become QueueSpec settings.
Bytes in, bytes out becomes typed payloads through a Codec.

column7: nothing to write: every publish is confirmed; send() returns once the broker has it
column8: Async confirm bookkeeping can be deleted.
Mandatory is the default.
Ack after the handler returns; a throw goes to the retry ladder.

column7: handler return = ack; AceRetryableException = retry; AceFatalException = dead-letter
column8: requeue=true loops on a poison message today; AceMQ retries with delays, then dead-letters.

column7: none: consume the queue instead of polling it
column8: A basic.get loop has no prefetch and no back-pressure.
Offsets are tracked by the reader.
JNDI lookups go; configuration names the broker.
A JMS queue is an AMQP queue on the default exchange; a topic becomes a topic exchange.

column7: mq.publisher(...) for sends; mq.consume(...) for receives
typed payloads through a Codec (JsonCodec by default)
column8: ObjectMessage (Java serialization) has no equivalent on purpose; pick a schema.

column7: none: route with a headers or topic exchange binding instead of a selector
column8: Selectors filter on the consumer; AMQP routes on the broker.

column7: none: use the outbox for publish-with-database; consume is at-least-once with the idempotent consumer
column8: XA has no equivalent.
